title: Inverse mates of invertible squares along equivalences are invertible
statement:
theorem isIso_inverseMate_of_equivalences
    {C : Type u₁} {D : Type u₂} {E : Type u₃} {F : Type u₄}
    [Category.{v₁} C] [Category.{v₂} D] [Category.{v₃} E] [Category.{v₄} F]
    {G : C ⥤ E} {H : D ⥤ F} [G.IsEquivalence] [H.IsEquivalence]
    {L₁ : C ⥤ D} {R₁ : D ⥤ C} {L₂ : E ⥤ F} {R₂ : F ⥤ E}
    (adj₁ : L₁ ⊣ R₁) (adj₂ : L₂ ⊣ R₂)
    (beta : R₁ ⋙ G ≅ H ⋙ R₂) :
    IsIso (((mateEquiv adj₁ adj₂).symm beta.hom).natTrans)

source.place: Tag 0B65; the natural Hom-bijection proof, with Mathlib Adjunction.Mates.unit_mateEquiv_symm

proof.text: For x and z choose z0=H.inv(z) with counit isomorphism H(z0) to z. Full faithfulness of H, adj1, full faithfulness of G, beta(z0), and adj2 give a bijection Hom(H(L1(x)),z) to Hom(L2(G(x)),z).
The inverse-mate unit equation and naturality of beta identify this bijection with precomposition by the inverse-mate component alpha(x).

Surjectivity at z=L2(G(x)) gives a left inverse of alpha(x); injectivity at z=H(L1(x)) gives the other inverse equation. Thus every component is invertible, hence alpha is invertible. This is the checked Mathlib isIso_of_coyoneda_map_bijective argument.

mathlib_searches.query: A square of right adjoints commuting with equivalences induces a left adjoint isomorphism compatible with units
mathlib_searches.results: Generic composition and adjunction tools; no exact inverse-mate invertibility theorem.

mateEquiv, unit_mateEquiv_symm and iterated_mateEquiv_conjugateEquiv_symm supply the mate and unit equation. The last gives a composite-transport alternative, not this immediate invertibility statement.

Mathlib Adjunction.Mates supplies mate and conjugate tools; no inverse-mate equivalence invertibility theorem. Upstream isIso_map_mateEquiv_app_of_isIso proves a related forward-mate result for fully faithful left adjoints.
